text:
on "the wilderness years" / the Badlands / re: "idk what to do with my life"

1/3

in a lot of bios, whether it be teddy roosevelt or churchill, u always see a period of 6 months to 2-3 years where they're sort of just off on their own

like TR, after losing his wife and mother in the same day, just bounces to the Badlands and spends a few years kicking it out west with cowboys and shedding the privileged-ness of his upbringing

he credits that to his becoming president, his ability to connect with the common man, and to earn respect independent of the harvard/porcellian image (which can be more of a negative than positive)

2/3

for someone in their early 20's / on the come-up, most advice is pretty straightfoward, at least in the NYC realm...like go do banking, get some pedigree, or go work at Google, just serve a few years in the corporatocracy whether u want to or not, it matters

but sometimes I get DMs from guys in 30s or 40s like, I did that, now I don't know what to do

my reply is always: u are exactly where u should be.

the idea that everything is up and to the right forever, becomes exposed as a fallacy pretty fast...usually around 35-40 there is an "up and out" in most industries

i.e. u become a MD/partner and lock in until age 60, or u go off solo, or u dont make the cut, or u say "fuck this shit"

all lead to, what do I do next

3/3

I prob need to do an article on this w/ a lot more case studies re: "wilderness years" but it almost seems like an imperative or a prerequisite for reaching ones potential, that u sort of just bounce for 6+ months and figure urself out

this means being willing to come back as someone different, which makes ppl uncomfortable

it also means that ur current social circles, u may realize they're not right for u...outgrowing old friends...being judged for "going off the path," etc

so people get stuck between -- do I stay miserable where I'm at, or risk the unknown. and for a lot of ppl, inertia wins out and they choose the former

END

ur best guide here is probably 1x1, behind closed doors, with someone u trust who is in their 50s-60s or higher

like, I can identify the dynamic, but someone that age will have firsthand experience + experience of 20 other ppl they've seen, and how this played out

they'll prob tell u the same, not to sweat "idk what I'm doing" - like, thats the default state lol. a life trajectory is less "up and to the right" than a bowling alley with those bumpers on each side, where u sort of careen back and forth until the lucky few find their mission...and once u do, boom, u ride that until u die.

but if u gotta go into the wilderness, or off to the Badlands to find it...then go to the Badlands.
